lead: Start from a random walk whose volatility depends on rank and add one feature at a time. Two additions do most of the work. Separating passing noise from lasting change removes 66% of the error, and giving each endpoint a home to return to removes a third of what is left. With short-lived swings added, 22% of the starting error remains. The later features move the summary far less and not always down: endpoint amplitude raises the error as scored here, and the full frozen stacks finish at 17%.
ladder_caption: Primary weighting: Facebook interactions, Reddit comment karma and Reddit submission karma count one third each. Bars to the right show error removed; paler bars to the left show error added. The range in the last column is the 5th–95th percentile from resampling simulation seeds and gate splits. After the tails step the path forks: the long-horizon steps are fitted on full panels and enter only the macro score, and the forecasting steps enter only the movement score. Each side ends at the panel's frozen stack.
findings:
• Noise is the largest step on both goals on every data set. It cuts the held-out movement error by 59% to 80% and the macro error by 33% to 73%. Without it, a random walk that matches one week of movement predicts thirteen-week moves 3.7 to 6.5 times too large on the long panels.
  • A home is the second. It lowers the gate error by 19% to 42% on four of the five panels and is the largest macro step on Facebook (62%). On long submissions it backfires until the short-lived swings are added. With every passing change treated as white noise, the fitted pull toward home goes to the top of the search grid on 43% of the rank bands there, and the simulated 13-week rank autocorrelation is 0.10 against 0.60 in the data.
  • After those steps the held-out gate can barely separate the rungs. On Facebook the next five steps move it from 0.127 to 0.103, with split-to-split standard deviations of 0.014 to 0.050. On comments it keeps falling slowly, from 0.241 to 0.137; the largest late gain there comes when the amplitude is extended to the lasting part (−0.049 ± 0.035, better on 4 of 5 splits).
  • Endpoint amplitude raises the macro error on all five panels (4% to 25%), mostly through the variance block. The direction is the same everywhere; the seed bands separate cleanly only on long submissions. At that step the simulators scale only the passing components by the amplitude. The long-horizon steps more than recover the loss on the three long panels, mostly at the first of them. Whether scaling the lasting part from the start would avoid the loss was not tested here.
  • On Facebook the three-profile model of home plus noise has the lowest macro error on the ladder: 0.90 tolerance units against 1.09 for the full structure stack. Its top-1 share is 1.5 times the data's, against 2.8 times for the full stack. The full stack is better on the variance block (0.13 against 0.45) and on the 15-row scorecard (14 passes against 12). One caution: in the simple model the fitted pull toward home sits at the top of the search grid on 80% of Facebook's rank bands, so its reversion rate is a boundary value and not an identified estimate.
  • These scores leave out what amplitude and fat tails were added to match: the spread of volatility across endpoints (log-SD 0.69 to 1.12 in these panels) and the kurtosis of each endpoint's own changes. A model without them cannot produce either. A step that shows no gain here can still be required by the data.
composite_caption: Error left relative to the simple rank diffusion, log scale, primary weighting. The band on the combined line is the 5th–95th percentile from resampling simulation seeds and gate splits. At the long-horizon step only the macro score changes; at the last step only the movement score changes.
panels_note: The five data sets agree on the first step and differ after it. On Facebook, noise and home take the macro error from 3.5 to 0.9 tolerance units and the gate from 0.70 to 0.13, below the baseline of 0.145; the macro error then climbs to 1.8 as the head share overshoots, and the long-horizon steps bring it back to 1.1. On comments the long-horizon steps matter most after noise: they take the macro error from 1.35 to 0.86. On long submissions the gate is dominated by one moment, the change rate at rank 1, which is zero in three of the five test windows and 0.04 and 0.08 in the other two; starting the forecast from each endpoint's actual state takes the error from 0.295 to 0.194. The 30-week submissions panel reaches 0.27 on macro after two steps and has nothing left to gain. On Instagram the macro error never falls below 1.8: from the home step on, the simulated top-1 share is 2.0 to 3.7 times the data's, the same kind of residual as on Facebook.
repairs_note: A rank diffusion gets one-week movement roughly right on Facebook and then extrapolates it. On the three long panels its variance ratios at 13 weeks sit near 0.8 where the data show 0.14 to 0.20, and held-out 13-week moves come out several times too large. Noise repairs the horizon scaling. Home repairs rank stickiness everywhere and the ladder block on Facebook. The upper tail of movement, shown in the starred columns and not scored by the gate, is under-predicted by about 37% at 13 weeks on Facebook from the swings step onward, and neither amplitude nor fat tails changes that.
weights_note: The picture does not depend on the choice. Under all five, noise is the largest step and home the second, the amplitude step raises the combined error, and the top of the ladder sits between 16% and 19% of the starting error.

Cards are passes of 15 and mean churn error. The recorded gate values for four panels were run at the command-line default of 3 simulations per split; rerun as recorded today they reproduce to three decimals. At 20 simulations the same stacks score 0.02 to 0.06 lower on all four. That direction is what simulation noise would produce, since the baseline has none and the error is an absolute deviation, but the cause was not isolated here. At 20 reps the comments stack is below its baseline on 4 of 5 splits and the short-submissions stack on 5 of 5; the long-submissions stack is above its baseline on 3 of 5. The frozen reference values are unchanged. Re-recording them at 20 reps is the owner's decision.
limits_extra:
• On long submissions the gate is dominated by the change rate at rank 1, which is zero in three of five test windows and near zero in the other two, so its gate numbers are noisier than the others at every rung.
  • The amplitude step is the one the frozen simulators implement: it scales the passing components only. The stated model scales the lasting part too. A rung with the full amplitude directly after the swings step was not run.
